institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer:
I was drawn to go on exchange because I wanted to experience a very different geological setting. I wanted to go on exchange to northern Norway because it gives me the opportunity of taking courses within arctic geology which is of great interest to me. A lot of geological processes thought in geoscience studies is represented in Norway which is of great inspiration to me to be surrounded of. 
I also saw going on exchange as an opportunity to go on a personal journey by moving abroad away from a safe ordinary and safe everyday life. I wanted to go on exchange to experience other branches of geology and to open the door to work on more international projects in the future by networking and develop my English and Norwegian language.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to study and explore Arktis.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were put in national groups when we had the intro on UiT. I think that was a big mistake. I wish to connect more with other exchange students from other nationalities than people from my own country and most of all Norwegians.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was easy to find, but the dates of the intro were changed very short before the start. That was confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Non, no one to pick me up at the airport. No one telling me how the public transport works in the city, so i knew how to get around.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: So the orientation about the study was good, but not that we were put in groups of nationalities.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden webpage works bad. It wasent easy to signup for student housings on the webpage. Only when i called them after arrival they signed me up.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that they should call samskipnaden to be sure they are signed up for student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a sad surprise that there were no duvet and pillow in my room and neither anything for the kitchen. I hope that future exchange student wont experience that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There should be a deeper explanation on how to sign up for courses on the list of things to do when arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Long, confusing but good that deadline for registration was 1 of september, so there was some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An exchange supervisor from geovitenskab.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't manage to figure out the registration process my self. My exchange supervisor helped me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A video-explanation on how to regrister would be a great help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the courses i took at UiT. The bachelor programme is different from on Københavns Universitet. The courses at KU bachelor programme have more focus on traditional geology, whereas at UiT the courses on the bachelor is more a preparation to go into more geological subjects i would say. Therefore i took a lot of master courses, because i there found subjects that i haven't had before.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: See above answer

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same, just not in GEO-2012 (Geofarer) where the teaching was running as a "flipped class room".

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEO-2012, Geofarer
GEO-3104, Advanced Structural Geology
GEO-3111, Reconstructing Quaternary Marine Climate and Environments
GEO-3122, Micropalaeontology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
GEO-3104, Advanced Structural Geology
GEO-3111, Reconstructing Quaternary Marine Climate and Environments
GEO-3122, Micropalaeontology

I didnt like the structure of course to much in GEO-2012. I was probably because the physical missing of the teacher for the most time. If she was more present during the classes i think it would have worked better, and would have been easier to ask questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with all the offers from TSI and the price is super fair i think. Continue the very good work with TSI i had amazing experiences and meet a lot of nice and new people through the groups of TSI :) Yay

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: TSI offer a lot of sport activities. Samskipnaden offers trips and social activities which is very nice, and the city offers a lot of cultural experiences.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: TSI, Samskipnaden trips and social events posts on Facebook. I also recommend to be a volunteer at either DRIV or a festival.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting students to download UT app to get an overview of the hiking opportunitets in the area. The app gives informations about the hike such as the level of challenge, transportation and time. I recommend students to reach out and find people to go on hikes with.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is very easy for me as a dane to adjust to the norwegian culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Reach out and ask for tips and social events. But also look up events on facebook and then ask your classmate to follow you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I find the relationship between nature and norwegians being more strong than for danes. they apprisiate their surroundings and thats is understandable. I great pleasure to experience the nature with norwegians. I also think norwegians has a very strong agenda on physical and mental well-being. I felt very good taking care of by the university and the student network and TSI.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: See answer above

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient in the beginning, there is a lot of things to figure out, but it will be okay. You are not alone. 
2. Enjoy. get out in the nature. Say yes to all the experiences you are ready to take. 
3. Ask all the questions you like.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the things i learned from the courses and the friends i got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To figure out things me self, where to live, to get new friends, to register on the university and to study for the exam.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
